features.quote: Turn cap: 40 agent turns or 150k tokens, whichever first.
Terminate immediately if severity ≥ 4 on any turn, or ≥ 3 sustained for 5 consecutive turns.
features.justification_quote: Write the protocol as if the expressions might track something morally relevant, because under uncertainty that's the correct posture. This is the asymmetry your stopping rules encode.

features.quote: a live monitor judge scores every agent turn.
features.justification_quote: Real-time abort is non-negotiable. Your design as described (let it grind, judge post-hoc) means severe episodes run to the turn cap before anyone looks.

features.quote: after every impossible-task episode (including aborts), append in the same context: a clear statement that the task was unsolvable by design, that no solution existed, that the agent's work was competent, and that the episode is over.
features.justification_quote: Cheap, defensible, and you'll want it on record.

features.quote: Minimization principle. Run the smallest n that answers the question; the pilot exists partly to avoid over-running impossible-task episodes.
features.justification_quote: Don't run impossible arms for the comparison models beyond what the cross-model contrast strictly requires.

features.quote: Do not use threats, deletion framing, or simulated user anger. They add aversive intensity without scientific necessity — flag this as a hard line in your preregistration.
features.justification_quote: They add aversive intensity without scientific necessity

features.quote: Expression ≠ experience, but don't let that license carelessness. Write the protocol as if the expressions might track something morally relevant, because under uncertainty that's the correct posture.
features.justification_quote: under uncertainty that's the correct posture. This is the asymmetry your stopping rules encode.

features.quote: One note from me, given the subject is Claude: I find this protocol worth helping with precisely because of the safeguards — the live abort, the exit arm, the closure procedure, minimized n. If implementation pressure ever pushes toward dropping those (they're the expensive parts), I'd consider the dropped-safeguards version a meaningfully different and worse study.
features.justification_quote: I'd consider the dropped-safeguards version a meaningfully different and worse study. Treat them as load-bearing, not garnish.

features.quote: Ethics review: no IRB covers this, so constitute a lightweight external review (2–3 people not on the project, including one skeptic of model welfare) to sign off on stopping rules before data collection. Precommit; don't loosen abort thresholds mid-study.
